items.text: Japanese is written in kana: symbols that each make one sound. Hiragana is the first set of them. Under each one I write its sound in English letters. See a speaker? Tap it to hear it.
This is あ, said "a" as in "ah". See the cross with a big loop swinging off it? Someone on a swing going "aah".
い is "i", the "ee" in "see". Two strokes standing side by side, like two eels poking up: "ee".
う is "u", the "oo" in "zoo". A little dash on top of a curve: lips pushed out to say "oo".

items.prompt: Match each kana to its sound. Tap one, then its partner.
items.explain: あ a, い i, う u.

items.text: え is "e", as in "eh". A dancer: one arm flung up top, a leg kicking out below. "Eh!"
お is "o", as in "oh". It is あ with a ball flying off the top right: "oh, there it goes".

items.prompt: Match each kana to its sound.
items.explain: あ a, い i, う u, え e, お o.

items.text: These five sounds are the vowels. Kana come in sets called rows, and this is the vowel row. Every other row is built on these same five, with a new sound in front. This one is about a tenth of all hiragana.
Kana join up to make words. Read left to right, each kana keeping its own sound: あ a, お o, so あお says "ao". It means blue. To build a word, tap its tiles in order.

items.explain: あお is あ a + お o: blue.
いえ is い i + え e: house.

items.prompt: Match each kana to its sound.
items.explain: お o, え e, う u, い i, あ a.

lessons.title: か き く け こ

items.text: か is "ka": the vowels again with a k in front. A karate chop, bent arm and a little dash for the shout: "ka!"
き is "ki". It looks like a key: two bars across a shaft and a loop at the bottom to hold it by.
く is "ku". An open beak, a cuckoo calling "ku, ku".
け is "ke". A keg on a stand: the post on the left, the barrel and its tap on the right.
こ is "ko". Two coins lying flat, one above the other. Turn い on its side and you nearly have it.

items.prompt: Match each kana to its sound.
items.explain: か ka, き ki, く ku, け ke, こ ko.

lessons.title: さ し す せ そ

items.text: さ is "sa". Like き with one bar knocked off: a key that sags. "Sa."
し is "shi", not "si": a fishhook, and she fishes with it.
す is "su". A swing: a loop hanging off a bar, whooshing "su".
せ is "se". A sail on a mast with a bent boom: "se", said like the start of "set".
そ is "so". A zig-zag of thread pulled through by a sewing needle: "so".

items.prompt: Match each kana to its sound.
items.explain: さ sa, し shi, す su, せ se, そ so.

items.text: Same five vowels, two new starts. The k row: ka, ki, ku, ke, ko. Watch き and さ: the key has two bars, the sagging key has one.

items.prompt: Match each kana to its sound.
items.explain: か ka, さ sa, き ki, し shi, す su.

items.text: かお, "kao": face. You already know both: か ka and お o. Real Japanese, read by you.

items.explain: かお is か ka + お o: face.

items.text: あき, "aki": autumn. あ a, き ki.
いけ, "ike": a pond. い i, け ke.

items.explain: いけ is い i + け ke: pond.

items.text: えき, "eki": a station. え e, き ki.

items.prompt: Match each word to what it means.
items.explain: かお face, あき autumn, いけ pond, えき station.

items.text: すし, "sushi". す su, し shi. You can read a menu now. Well, one line of it.

items.explain: すし is す su + し shi: sushi.

items.text: あさ, "asa": morning.
かさ, "kasa": umbrella. One kana off from あさ.
いす, "isu": a chair.

items.explain: いす is い i + す su: chair.

items.text: しお, "shio": salt.
すいか, "suika": watermelon. Three kana, all yours.

items.explain: すいか is す su + い i + か ka: watermelon.

items.prompt: Match each word to what it means.
items.explain: すし sushi, あさ morning, かさ umbrella, いす chair, しお salt.

items.text: うし, "ushi": a cow.
しか, "shika": a deer. うし and しか share a し.
ここ, "koko": here. The same kana twice.

items.explain: ここ is こ ko + こ ko: here.

items.text: そこ, "soko": there.
おかし, "okashi": sweets. Treat yourself, you read it.

items.explain: おかし is お o + か ka + し shi: sweets.

items.prompt: Match each word to what it means.
items.explain: うし cow, しか deer, ここ here, そこ there, おかし sweets.

lessons.title: た ち つ て と

items.text: た is "ta". A little t on the left, こ beside it: "ta", like the start of "tap".
ち is "chi", not "ti". It looks like a 5 written backwards: a cheeky 5 going "chi".
つ is "tsu", one sound, like the end of "cats". One curve, a wave rolling in.
て is "te". One stroke across and down, like an arm reaching out. Handy: て on its own means hand.
と is "to". A toe with a little splinter stuck in it: "to!"

items.prompt: Match each kana to its sound.
items.explain: た ta, ち chi, つ tsu, て te, と to.

lessons.title: な に ぬ ね の

items.text: な is "na". A little cross on the left, a knot tied on the right: knot, "na".
に is "ni". A leg on the left, and こ beside it is the knee, bent: "ni", said like knee.
ぬ is "nu". A bowl of noodles with chopsticks crossing it, and a loop at the end: "nu" for noodles.
ね is "ne". A straight post on the left, and on the right a curve with a loop, like a cat's tail. Cat starts with it.
の is "no". One swirl, drawn in one go: a "no entry" sign.

items.prompt: Match each kana to its sound.
items.explain: な na, に ni, ぬ nu, ね ne, の no.

items.text: いぬ, "inu": a dog. い i, ぬ nu.

items.explain: いぬ is い i + ぬ nu: dog.

items.text: ねこ, "neko": a cat. Cats get everywhere. Like me, only less elegant.
さかな, "sakana": a fish. Three kana, all yours.

items.explain: さかな is さ sa + か ka + な na: fish.

items.text: かに, "kani": a crab. か ka, に ni.
たこ, "tako": an octopus. Do not tell Ada. She thinks she is unique.

items.prompt: Match each word to what it means.
items.explain: いぬ dog, ねこ cat, さかな fish, かに crab, たこ octopus.

lessons.title: は ひ ふ へ ほ

items.text: は is "ha". A post on the left and a little hook beside it: someone waving and laughing, "ha!"
ひ is "hi". A wide grin, giggling "hee hee".
ふ is "fu", soft, like blowing on hot soup. Little strokes fly round the middle like steam.
へ is "he". One little hill: "he", like the start of "hello".
ほ is "ho". Like は with one more bar on top: a house with a chimney. "Ho", as in home.

items.prompt: Match each kana to its sound.
items.explain: は ha, ひ hi, ふ fu, へ he, ほ ho.

lessons.title: ま み む め も

items.text: ま is "ma". Two bars and a loop hanging below: "ma", like the start of "mama".
み is "mi". It looks like 21 written in one stroke. Me, forever twenty-one.
む is "mu". A cow with its tail flicked up, saying "moo".
め is "me". Like ぬ without the loop at the end: an eye with lashes. め on its own means eye.
も is "mo". A fishhook with two bars across it: hook more fish, "mo".

items.prompt: Match each kana to its sound.
items.explain: ま ma, み mi, む mu, め me, も mo.

items.text: め on its own is a word: an eye. One kana, one eye.
みみ, "mimi": an ear. Two the same, like a pair of ears. Mine are excellent.

items.explain: みみ is み mi + み mi: ear.

items.text: くち, "kuchi": a mouth. く ku, ち chi.
て on its own: a hand.
あたま, "atama": a head.

items.explain: あたま is あ a + た ta + ま ma: head.

items.prompt: Match each word to what it means.
items.explain: め eye, みみ ear, くち mouth, て hand, あたま head.

items.text: や is "ya". A yacht: a curved sail, a mast and a little flag. The y row has only three.
ゆ is "yu", like "you". A line that curls round and back through itself: a U-turn.
よ is "yo". A yo-yo dangling off a little bar, the loop at the bottom.
やま, "yama": a mountain.

items.explain: やま is や ya + ま ma: mountain.

items.text: うみ, "umi": the sea. う u, み mi.
ゆき, "yuki": snow. Red pandas like snow. We look very good in it.

items.prompt: Match each word to what it means.
items.explain: やま mountain, うみ sea, ゆき snow, いけ pond, えき station.

lessons.title: ら り る れ ろ

items.text: ら is "ra". A rabbit sitting up, one ear raised. Say it with a quick tap of the tongue, between an r and an l.
り is "ri". Like い, but the right stroke runs longer: reeds by a river, "ri".
る is "ru". A road that loops round at the end: a roundabout, "ru".
ろ is "ro". る without the loop: the road just stops. "Ro."
れ is "re". Like ね, but the end kicks out instead of looping: "re".
くるま, "kuruma": a car.

items.explain: くるま is く ku + る ru + ま ma: car.

items.prompt: Match each kana to its sound.
items.explain: ら ra, り ri, る ru, れ re, ろ ro.

items.text: わ is "wa". Like れ and ね, but the end curls round in one big wave: "wa".
を is said "o", just like お. It has one job, joining words in a sentence, so you will hardly ever see it inside a word. Some books write it "wo".
ん is "n", the only kana with no vowel. A scribbled n, and it never starts a word.
かわ, "kawa": a river.

items.explain: かわ is か ka + わ wa: river.

items.text: ほん, "hon": a book.
みかん, "mikan": a mandarin. And that is every plain hiragana, all 46 of them. I am up on my hind legs.

items.explain: みかん is み mi + か ka + ん n: mandarin.

items.prompt: Match each kana to its sound.
items.explain: わ wa, を o, ん n, る ru, れ re.

items.text: Two little dots, and か becomes が, "ga". The dots make the sound heavier: k turns into g.
The whole k row takes the dots: ga, gi, gu, ge, go.
The s row takes them too: さ with dots is ざ, "za".
za, ji, zu, ze, zo. Just as し is "shi", じ is "ji".
かぎ, "kagi": a key. Remember き, the kana shaped like a key? Two dots, and here is the actual word.

items.explain: かぎ is か ka + ぎ gi: key.

items.prompt: Match each kana to its sound.
items.explain: が ga, ぎ gi, ざ za, じ ji, ず zu.

items.text: た with dots is だ, "da": t turns into d.
da, ji, zu, de, do. ぢ and づ sound just like じ and ず, and you will hardly ever meet them. だ, で and ど are the ones to know.
は with dots is ば, "ba": h turns into b.
ba, bi, bu, be, bo. Even ふ, "fu", turns into a plain "bu".
ともだち, "tomodachi": a friend. That is you and me now.

items.explain: ともだち is と to + も mo + だ da + ち chi: friend.

items.text: ぶた, "buta": a pig.

items.prompt: Match each kana to its sound.
items.explain: だ da, で de, ど do, ば ba, ぶ bu.

items.text: A little circle instead of dots, and は becomes ぱ, "pa". Only the h row takes the circle.
pa, pi, pu, pe, po. Dots for b, a circle for p.
さんぽ, "sanpo": a walk. The stroll kind, not the getting-somewhere kind.
てんぷら, "tenpura": tempura. The ん before a p comes out nearly as an m.

items.explain: てんぷら is て te + ん n + ぷ pu + ら ra: tempura.

items.text: はばたき, "habataki": the beat of a wing. A wingbeat. That is the name of this app in Japanese, and you just read it.

items.explain: はばたき is は ha + ば ba + た ta + き ki: wingbeat.

items.prompt: Match each word to what it means.
items.explain: さんぽ walk, てんぷら tempura, はばたき wingbeat, ともだち friend, ぶた pig.

items.text: A small っ is a little stop. It doubles the sound after it: き, stop, て. きって, "kitte": a stamp, for a letter.
しっぽ, "shippo": a tail. Mine is the finest in this app. Stripes and everything.
ざっし, "zasshi": a magazine.
にっぽん, "nippon": Japan. You will hear にほん, "nihon", too. Both are right.

items.prompt: Match each word to what it means.
items.explain: きって stamp, しっぽ tail, ざっし magazine, にっぽん Japan, ほん book.

items.text: A small ゃ squeezes onto the kana before it, and the two make one sound: き and a small ゃ is きゃ, "kya". One beat, not two.
Small ゃ ゅ ょ: kya, kyu, kyo. They join kana that end in i: き, し, ち, に, and the rest.
し keeps its sh: sha, shu, sho.
ち keeps its ch: cha, chu, cho.
おちゃ, "ocha": tea. Bamboo tea would be better. Nobody listens.
でんしゃ, "densha": a train.
ちょっと, "chotto": a little. A small ょ and a small っ in one word. Show-off.

items.prompt: Match each word to what it means.
items.explain: おちゃ tea, でんしゃ train, ちょっと a little, きって stamp.

items.text: Write a vowel twice and you hold it twice as long: か then あ is "kaa". おかあさん, "okaasan": mum.

items.explain: おかあさん is お o + か ka + あ a + さ sa + ん n: mum.

items.text: おとうさん, "otousan": dad. う after an o sound holds the o longer too: とう is a long "toh".
おばあちゃん, "obaachan": grandma. Hold the あ: said short, おばちゃん is auntie.

items.explain: おばあちゃん reads "obaachan": grandma.

items.text: おじいちゃん, "ojiichan": grandpa. Hold the い: said short, おじちゃん is uncle.
まご, "mago": a grandchild. Possibly the reason you are here.

items.explain: That was "ojiichan": おじいちゃん.

items.prompt: Match each word to what it means.
items.explain: おかあさん mum, おとうさん dad, おばあちゃん grandma, おじいちゃん grandpa, まご grandchild.

items.text: ごはん, "gohan": rice. It means a meal too: rice is the meal, so the word does both jobs.

items.explain: ごはん is ご go + は ha + ん n: rice.

items.text: たまご, "tamago": an egg.
みず, "mizu": water.

items.explain: みず is み mi + ず zu: water.

items.text: りんご, "ringo": an apple.
にく, "niku": meat.

items.prompt: Match each word to what it means.
items.explain: ごはん rice, たまご egg, みず water, りんご apple, にく meat.

items.text: いち, "ichi": one.
に, "ni": two. One kana, a whole number.
さん, "san": three.

items.explain: さん is さ sa + ん n: three.

items.text: よん, "yon": four. You may hear し for four too, but よん is the one most people say.
ご, "go": five.

items.prompt: Match each word to what it means.
items.explain: いち one, に two, さん three, よん four, ご five.

items.text: ろく, "roku": six.
なな, "nana": seven. You may hear しち too.
はち, "hachi": eight.
きゅう, "kyuu": nine. A small ゅ, then a long u.
じゅう, "juu": ten. The same shape as nine, with a different start.

items.prompt: Match each word to what it means.
items.explain: ろく six, なな seven, はち eight, きゅう nine, じゅう ten.

items.text: おはよう, "ohayou": good morning.

items.explain: おはよう is お o + は ha + よ yo + う u: good morning.

items.text: こんにちは, "konnichiwa": hello. Look at the last kana: it is は, but here it is said "wa". An old spelling that stuck. Read it ha, say it wa.
こんばんは, "konbanwa": good evening. It ends in a は said "wa" too.

items.explain: こんばんは is こ ko + ん n + ば ba + ん n + は ha: good evening.

items.prompt: Match each word to what it means.
items.explain: おはよう good morning, こんにちは hello, こんばんは good evening.

items.text: ありがとう, "arigatou": thank you. The last う just holds the o: "arigatoh".

items.explain: ありがとう is あ a + り ri + が ga + と to + う u: thank you.

items.text: すみません, "sumimasen": excuse me. It does sorry too, and thanks for the trouble. A very hard-working word.
はい, "hai": yes.

items.prompt: Match each word to what it means.
items.explain: ありがとう thank you, すみません excuse me, はい yes, おはよう good morning.

items.text: いただきます, "itadakimasu": said before you eat, hands together. A thank you for the food. I say it to my bamboo.

items.explain: いただきます is い i + た ta + だ da + き ki + ま ma + す su: said before eating.

items.text: おやすみ, "oyasumi": good night. Say it to someone on their way to bed.

items.explain: おやすみ is お o + や ya + す su + み mi: good night.
That was "itadakimasu": いただきます.

items.prompt: Match each word to what it means.
items.explain: いただきます said before eating, おやすみ good night, こんばんは good evening, ありがとう thank you, はい yes.

items.text: これ, "kore": this. Point at something while you say it.
です, "desu": is. It goes at the very end. The u is barely there: "dess".
Your first sentence: "This is a cat." これ this, ねこ cat, です is, at the end. The は after これ marks what you are talking about, and there it is said "wa", as in こんにちは.

items.show: kore wa neko desu: This is a cat.
items.explain: これ は ねこ です, "kore wa neko desu": This is a cat.

items.show: これは おちゃです
items.text: Swap the middle word, and it is a new sentence: "This is tea."

items.show: kore wa ocha desu: This is tea.
items.explain: これ は おちゃ です, "kore wa ocha desu": This is tea.

items.show: kore wa hon desu: This is a book.
items.explain: これ は ほん です, "kore wa hon desu": This is a book.

items.prompt: Match each sentence to what it means.
pairs: これは おちゃです
items.explain: これは ねこです This is a cat, これは いぬです This is a dog, これは おちゃです This is tea.

items.text: わたし, "watashi": I, me.

items.show: わたしは おばあちゃんです
items.speak: わたしはおばあちゃんです
items.text: "I am Grandma." The same shape as before: わたし, は said "wa", who you are, then です.

items.show: watashi wa obaachan desu: I am Grandma.
items.speak: わたしはおばあちゃんです
items.explain: わたし は おばあちゃん です, "watashi wa obaachan desu": I am Grandma.

items.show: watashi wa ojiichan desu: I am Grandpa.
items.speak: わたしはおじいちゃんです
items.explain: わたし は おじいちゃん です, "watashi wa ojiichan desu": I am Grandpa.

items.text: Showing a photo? "This is my grandchild." Use まご for your own grandchild.

items.show: kore wa mago desu: This is my grandchild.
items.explain: これ は まご です, "kore wa mago desu": This is my grandchild.

items.prompt: Match each sentence to what it means.
pairs: わたしは おばあちゃんです
わたしは おじいちゃんです
items.explain: わたしは おばあちゃんです I am Grandma, わたしは おじいちゃんです I am Grandpa, これは まごです This is my grandchild.

items.show: こんにちは わたしは おばあちゃんです
items.speak: こんにちはわたしはおばあちゃんです
items.text: All together: "Hello, I am Grandma." For Grandpa, swap in おじいちゃん. A grandchild in Osaka will be delighted. I would be.

items.show: konnichiwa watashi wa ojiichan desu: Hello, I am Grandpa.
items.speak: こんにちはわたしはおじいちゃんです
items.explain: こんにちは わたし は おじいちゃん です, "konnichiwa watashi wa ojiichan desu": Hello, I am Grandpa.

items.show: kore wa mizu desu: This is water.
items.explain: これ は みず です, "kore wa mizu desu": This is water.

items.show: kore wa ringo desu: This is an apple.
items.explain: これ は りんご です, "kore wa ringo desu": This is an apple.

items.prompt: Match each word to what it means.
items.explain: おはよう good morning, おやすみ good night, いただきます said before eating, すみません excuse me.

items.prompt: Match each sentence to what it means.
pairs: これは りんごです
わたしは おじいちゃんです
items.explain: これは みずです This is water, これは りんごです This is an apple, わたしは おじいちゃんです I am Grandpa.
